issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וַיִּקַּח מִן הַבָּא בְיָדוֹ' means 'he took from what came into his hand' (i.e., from what he had with him), but the Chinese '從他手中拿了一份' says 'took a portion from his hand,' which changes the subject/possession: in Hebrew, the items are in Jacob's hand (his possession), not in Esau's hand. The Chinese could be misread as taking from Esau's hand, altering who possesses the gift.
